text: Exploration notebooks live under `notebooks/scratch/` and are purged after 60 days.
Use pools to cap concurrent warehouse queries per DAG family.
Wrap warehouse connections in a context manager that closes on error.
Lineage is captured with OpenLineage events from Airflow and dbt.
Seed random generators; log the seed on failure.
Renaming or dropping a snapshot column needs a migration note in the PR.
Wildcard tables are banned in new code; use partitioned tables.
A doc older than 12 months without review gets a staleness label.
Enable `MFA` for every human user; service users are exempt but IP-restricted.
Copy datasets between regions with the transfer service, scheduled off-peak.
Internal wiki pages are for process; code behavior goes in the repo docs.
Idempotent loads: re-running a load for the same batch id must not duplicate rows.
Vendor API keys are issued to a shared team mailbox, not an individual.
Slim CI runs `dbt build --select state:modified+ --defer` against the prod manifest.
Weekly data digests summarize incidents, launches, and deprecations.
Row-level security is implemented with user attributes, never separate dashboards per region.
Teardown must run even when a test fails; use fixtures with `yield`.
Annual security training is required before production access is granted.
Singular dbt tests under `tests/` return failing rows, and each carries a comment explaining the business rule.
Dev warehouses are XS by default; request a size increase in #data-cost with a reason.
In staging models, wrap timestamps in `{{ to_utc('col') }}` and alias with `_at`; leave plain `date` columns alone.
Production database credentials are never available to developer laptops.
Document macro arguments in `macros/_macros.yml` so `dbt docs` renders them.
Review metric changes with a before-and-after comparison table.
Metrics-layer models are `metric_<name>` and live in `models/metrics/`.
Dataset IAM is managed in Terraform; console edits are reverted nightly.
Query tags identify the tool and job: `dbt:<invocation_id>`, `airflow:<dag_id>`.
Breaking changes to a contracted model ship as a new `_v2` version with a 90-day deprecation window for the old one.
Python UDFs need a review from platform; prefer SQL UDFs.
Dataset `analytics` has an owner label and a documented retention in `bigquery/datasets.yml`.
Sample failing rows are stored for 7 days for debugging, in a restricted schema.
Least privilege: request the narrowest role and a time limit for elevated access.
Default table expiration on new datasets is set at creation in Terraform.
Escalate to the platform lead if a Sev1 lasts over two hours.
Data SLAs are published on the catalog page for each mart.
CDC pipelines record the log position so a restart resumes exactly where it stopped.
Analyses start with a header comment naming the requester, the ticket id and the date.
Notebook parameters (dates, schema names) go in the first code cell, tagged `parameters`.
Write the runbook before the launch, not after the first incident.
The `Customer Health` dashboard is reviewed quarterly by its owner; stale tiles are removed.
`MERGE` statements filter the target by partition to prune scans.
Mart models expected to exceed 50M rows are materialized `incremental` with a `unique_key` and a 3-day lookback.
Retention reviews quarterly: drop or archive tables not read in 90 days.
Review slot usage for `finance_ro` jobs monthly and tag outliers in #data-cost.
Tag every database with `cost_center` so the chargeback report works.
SLAs are defined with `sla_miss_callback` only for tier-1 DAGs.
Macros that take more than three arguments use keyword arguments at every call site.
Request access via the IdP group, not by pinging admins.
Dashboards are named `<Domain> - <Question>`.
Tag every mart model with its business domain (`finance`, `growth` or `ops`).
Quote any lookup seed value that contains a comma, and run `csvlint` in pre-commit.
Null-rate monitors protect join keys on marts; thresholds live in code.
Log queries by role and flag access to PII tables outside business hours.
Contracts reference the glossary term for every business field.
Row-level security tests run in CI for tenant-isolated schemas.
Back up the snapshot schema before changing a snapshot's `strategy` or `unique_key`.
Review slot usage for `raw_events` jobs monthly and tag outliers in #data-cost.
DAG files import nothing heavy at module level; imports happen inside tasks to keep parse time under 1s.
Cross-team contracts are reviewed in the monthly data-governance sync.
Every `fct_` model states its grain in the YAML description as `Grain: one row per ...`, and a unique test on the surrogate key backs it.
When a vendor feed arrives late, notify consumers at 2 hours late, not when it is fixed.
Every repo has a README with purpose, setup, and an owner.
Large binaries go to object storage, not git; the pre-commit hook rejects files over 1 MB.
Lineage must reach the BI layer; broken lineage is a ticket for platform.
Prefer `jupytext` percent format for notebooks that need code review.
Favor reversible decisions; document the ones that are not.
A snapshot that exceeds 200M rows moves to an `incremental` history model with a `merge` strategy.
The `Executive KPIs` dashboard is reviewed quarterly by its owner; stale tiles are removed.
Developer schemas expire automatically after 14 days; extending one needs a note in the ticket.
Deprecate a macro by keeping it for one release with a `log(..., info=True)` warning that names its replacement.
Never grant `SUPERUSER`; use `pg_read_all_data` for read-only investigations.
Test a macro on both Snowflake and BigQuery before merging when it uses date functions.
Environment-specific settings come from `Settings()` reading env vars, never from `if prod:` branches.
Extensions are installed by the platform team through Terraform, not by developers.
Keep example outputs short and mark truncated parts with an ellipsis.
Do not run `dbt run --full-refresh` on an incremental mart in production without a ticket and an owner on call.
Do not push directly to release branches; open a PR targeting them.
Keep macros under 60 lines; extract helpers when a macro grows past that.
Handoffs are written down; no tribal knowledge in DMs.
Use `pg_stat_statements` and review the top 10 by total time weekly.
If the source has `_is_deleted`, add `where not _is_deleted` in the renamed CTE and do not select the column.
Rate-limit vendor APIs with token buckets; respect `Retry-After` headers.
Use a `concurrency` group keyed on the branch with `cancel-in-progress: true`.
Warehouse role grants are renamed by creating the new role, re-granting, then dropping the old role after a week.
Quality results are written to `ops.dq_results` and graphed on the data health dashboard.
Use `tenacity` for retries around API calls; no hand-written sleep loops.
The staging bucket for vendor file drops keeps files 14 days; a lifecycle rule purges older files.
Use `TaskFlow` decorators for new Python tasks; avoid `PythonOperator` boilerplate.
Docs are updated in the same PR as the code they describe.
Developer sandboxes are created with zero-copy `CLONE` of production, not by reloading data.
Streaming inserts are only for the events pipeline; batch loads use load jobs.
Every resource has `team`, `env`, and `cost_center` tags.
Tag datasets with their domain and tier; tier-1 datasets require on-call coverage.
Use SSO with MFA for every human login to data platforms.
Report cost per dashboard load for the top 10 dashboards in the monthly review.
Lookup seeds are loaded with `dbt seed --select tag:lookup` before any model build in CI.
Tasks retry 3 times with `retry_exponential_backoff=True`; never retry non-idempotent tasks.
`Executive KPIs` tiles cite the mart they read from in the tile description.
Spell out acronyms on first use in each document.
Use authorized views to share data across projects instead of copying tables.
Time dimensions declare their smallest grain explicitly.
Grant privileges to roles, never directly to users, and name roles `<env>_<domain>_<access>` such as `prod_finance_read`.
Local setup is a single `make setup`; if it needs more steps, fix the Makefile.
Dimension labels are Title Case; measures say what they count: `Active Customers`.
Clear notebook outputs with `nbstripout` in pre-commit; outputs never land in git.
Deprecated datasets show a banner in the catalog and a removal date.
Use `on_failure_callback` to page only tier-1 DAGs; tier-2 posts to #data-alerts.
Document each vendor's rate limits next to the client code.
Maintenance windows are announced 48 hours ahead with an end time.
Airflow variables are read inside tasks, not at DAG parse time.
`DEV_WH` has a dedicated resource monitor and an owner listed in `snowflake/warehouses.yml`.
Terraform state lives in the remote backend with locking; never run apply from a laptop.
Tasks that load data are idempotent and get `retries=2` with exponential backoff; non-idempotent tasks get `retries=0`.
Do not use pie charts with more than five slices.
Do not join two snapshots directly; materialize each to a dimension first.
Masking policies attach to tags, not to individual columns.
Set `maximum_bytes_billed` on every scheduled query and dbt profile.
Query snapshots through a `dim_*_history` view, not directly from BI.
Evaluation sets for LLM features are reviewed by a human before they gate releases.
Run `terraform fmt` and `tflint` in pre-commit.
Credentials reach DAGs through Airflow Connections, never through Variables or hard-coded strings.
Disable a retired DAG with `is_paused_upon_creation=True` for one cycle before deleting the file.
Window functions in marts get an explicit frame clause; defaults differ between warehouses.
Dimensions marked `primary` define the default time spine.
Load tests run before major launches against a production-sized clone.
Tag-based selection (`tag:nightly`) is the only scheduling interface for models.
Mock at the boundary (HTTP, warehouse client), not inside our own modules.
Bump the project `version` in `dbt_project.yml` only when a release tag is cut, never inside a feature PR.
Do not rewrite history on shared release branches.
Every DAG sets `catchup=False` unless a backfill is the explicit purpose.
Reports of suspected leaks go to security@ immediately, then #security-incident.
Latency SLOs in contracts use p95 and p99, not averages.
Anomaly alerts include a link to the lineage graph and the last passing run.
Use `trigger_rule='none_failed_min_one_success'` after branch operators.
Python utilities carry type hints and are formatted with `ruff format` before commit.
Set `dagrun_timeout` on every DAG to twice its p95 runtime.
Schemas for marts are domain names: `finance`, `growth`, `ops`.
A deploy workflow requires a manual approval from the `data-release` environment reviewers.
Macro files are named after the macro they define, one macro per file when it is public.
Use `.git-blame-ignore-revs` for mass-format commits.
Group names in dbt are the team names exactly as in the directory.
Glossary changes go through a monthly review with finance and product.
Metrics definitions are linked to the glossary page; no unexplained KPIs.
Content validation runs in CI for LookML: `lookml validate` plus the Content Validator.
Storage costs are reviewed monthly; clones older than seven days are dropped.
An analysis that is requested a second time is promoted to a mart model rather than copied between tickets.
Use `httpx` with explicit timeouts; the default is no timeout.
Kafka consumers commit offsets after the warehouse write succeeds, never before.
Alert on a snapshot whose latest `dbt_valid_from` is older than 36 hours.
Snapshot names are the entity in singular form.
A breaking contract change needs a new major version and 30 days of dual publishing.
Lookup seeds declare `+column_types` explicitly in the seeds YAML.
Review the incident count and mean time to detect in the monthly ops meeting.
Review IAM policies with `terraform plan` output attached to the PR.
Never share query results containing PII over Slack or email.
Encryption at rest and in transit is mandatory; use platform defaults, not custom crypto.
Every dashboard has an owner, a purpose line, and a review date in its description.
Workflows pin third-party actions to a full commit SHA, not a tag.
A near miss gets a short writeup too; learning is not limited to outages.
When a test needs more than 20 lines of setup, extract a builder.
Dimensional marts use `dim_<entity>`; bridge tables use `bridge_<a>_<b>`.
Data-quality checks run after load and before publish, and failures block publish.
Hotfix branches start from the last release tag, not main.
Upload `target/run_results.json` as an artifact on every dbt CI run.
Use `git commit --fixup` while addressing review so reviewers can follow changes.
Marts read upstream models through `ref()` only; if a mart needs a new upstream field, add it to the intermediate layer first.
Set budgets and alerts per team at 50%, 80%, and 100% of monthly allocation.
Run `dbt seed --full-refresh` only for lookup seeds whose column types changed.
An analysis is deleted after 90 days unless it has a linked ticket marked recurring.
Every workflow sets `permissions:` explicitly; the default is `contents: read`.
Every dashboard description names an owner and a refresh schedule, and unowned dashboards are archived after 60 days.
A failing tier-1 check blocks publish of the affected mart.
Keep transactions short; no network calls inside an open transaction.
Scripts that write to prod take `--dry-run` and default to it.
Delete dead code and dead tables; archive first if unsure.
yml files for dbt exposures and semantic models use two-space indentation and no anchors, so `dbt parse` errors stay readable.
Summarize long threads before asking for decisions.
Use `hard_deletes: new_record` on snapshots of tables that physically drop rows.
Unused service accounts and keys are removed in the quarterly access review to avoid idle spend.
Check `QUERY_HISTORY` for spilled-to-remote queries weekly and resize or rewrite them.
Retros produce at most three actions, each with an owner.
A red `main` blocks merges until fixed or reverted within one hour.
Track vendor renewals 90 days ahead in the contracts calendar.
Put commands in fenced code blocks with the shell prompt omitted so they can be copied.
Row access policies are managed in Terraform, never by ad hoc `ALTER` statements.
Event schemas in the registry use backward-compatible Avro evolution only.
Record the blast radius: affected tables, dashboards, and consumers.
Tag every compute resource with `cost_center` and `owner`.
Enum values are listed in the contract; adding one is minor, removing one is major.
Contract tests between producer and consumer run in both repos' CI.
Sev1: customer-facing data wrong or missing; page on-call immediately.
Alert thresholds are reviewed quarterly against false-positive rates.
`Customer Health` tiles cite the mart they read from in the tile description.
Roles are group roles with `NOLOGIN`; users inherit from them.
Sign commits on release branches; `git config commit.gpgsign true`.
Warehouses auto-suspend at 60 seconds; `BI_WH` at 300 for cache warmth.
Freshness monitors exist for every tier-1 mart and notify the owning team channel.
Cache the `uv` and `dbt packages` directories keyed on lock file hashes.
Group by ordinal positions are banned; name the columns.
Use incremental models for tables above 10M rows before asking for a bigger warehouse.
Pin dbt packages to exact versions in `packages.yml` and upgrade them in their own PR.
Do not commit analysis output CSVs; attach them to the ticket.
Training sets are materialized with a fixed as-of date and stored with the model artifact.
On-call handoff happens Monday 10:00 with a written summary of open issues.
Analyses are read-only SQL: no DDL, no DML and no temp tables.
Prefer explicit config over implicit defaults for anything affecting cost or security.
Contract validation failures block the producer's deploy, not the consumer's.
Document each connector's expected latency and which dashboards depend on it.
Network changes (VPC, peering) require a platform review.
Wide denormalized dashboard tables are named `rpt_<dashboard>` and are never joined back into other marts.
Design docs state non-goals explicitly.
Reconciliation checks compare mart totals to the finance system weekly.
Do not call `run_query` in a macro that runs at parse time; guard with `{% if execute %}`.
Each script's docstring states inputs, outputs, and who to ask.
Review `DEV_WH` utilization monthly and downsize if average queueing is zero.
Row-level access policies are added through Terraform modules, not scripts.
Run `pytest -x -q` before pushing; the full suite runs in CI.
Use `coalesce` rather than `ifnull` or `nvl` so SQL stays portable.
Matrix jobs set `fail-fast: false` so one failing warehouse does not hide others.
Dimension models carry `valid_from` and `valid_to` only when built from a snapshot; a plain dimension must not fake history columns.
Schema drift on a connector pauses the sync and alerts the owner before loading new columns.
Mart yml must list `data_tests` for accepted_values on every enum-like column.
CI uses `concurrency` groups so a new push cancels the older run on the same branch.
Dynamic tables set `TARGET_LAG` explicitly and are tagged with the owning team.
Review comments are resolved by the reviewer, not the author.
Row-count and null-rate checks have explicit thresholds in code, not magic numbers.
Set `max_active_runs=1` on DAGs that write to shared tables.
Semantic model names match their mart: `sm_fct_orders`.
Mark deprecated docs with a banner and a pointer to the replacement.
Mark deprecated lookup rows with `is_active = false` instead of deleting them.
Check bloat on `users` monthly with `pgstattuple` and schedule a repack if over 30%.
Lookup seeds are UTF-8 without BOM, LF line endings.
Large result sets are written to the `scratch` schema, not downloaded into the notebook.
A dashboard with PII needs a steward sign-off and masked columns by default.
Backfills run in partitions of at most 31 days, one after another.
Never print credentials; the logger redacts `password`, `token` and `secret` keys.
Only the platform team provisions new SaaS integrations to the warehouse.
Coverage must not drop on changed lines; the PR check enforces 80% for new code.
Metabase questions that are reused three times become saved models.
A DAG that calls dbt uses `cosmos` task groups, one group per dbt selector.
`BI_WH` has a dedicated resource monitor and an owner listed in `snowflake/warehouses.yml`.
Customer-visible incidents get a status page entry reviewed by support.
Delete scratch tables created by a notebook in its final cell.
Environment variables for dbt are prefixed `DBT_ENV_` and documented in the README.
Review `BI_WH` utilization monthly and downsize if average queueing is zero.
Prefer `union all` over `union` unless you need deduplication.
Offboarding removes access within 24 hours via the IdP deprovision workflow.
Use `logging`, not `print`, in anything that runs under a scheduler.
Count columns in marts end with `_count`; rate columns in marts end with `_rate`.
Tag every DAG with its owning team and tier (`tier-1`, `tier-2`).
Ratio metrics reference two existing measures instead of redefining them.
Use `secrets` from the vault client, not environment variables, for API tokens in jobs.
Analyses using sampled data say so in the header comment, with the sample rate.
Sort lookup seed rows by key so diffs stay small.
The `Marketing Funnel` dashboard is reviewed quarterly by its owner; stale tiles are removed.
Mart models end with a single `final` CTE followed by `select * from final`.
Pin direct dependencies in `pyproject.toml`; `uv lock` output is committed.
Scheduled queries run as the `bq-scheduler` service account, not a person.
Surrogate keys in marts come from `dbt_utils.generate_surrogate_key`; do not hand-roll `md5(concat(...))`.
Search optimization is enabled per table after a cost estimate in the PR.
Version bumps of dbt-core are rehearsed on a branch with the full CI suite.
Never force-push to `main` or to a branch someone else has reviewed.
Never grant `select` on a mart to `PUBLIC`; grant to the `reporting_ro` role in the post-hook.
Prefer vendors with SOC 2 Type II reports; store the latest report in the vault.
PR CI builds only modified models and their children (`state:modified+`) against the production manifest.
Assertions compare full values, not just lengths or truthiness.
Link the postmortem in the incident ticket and in the service's runbook.
`Ops Daily` tiles cite the mart they read from in the tile description.
Application queries use prepared statements through the driver, never string formatting.
Check cross-table consistency after major schema changes.
`ACCOUNTADMIN` is used only for billing and account-level setup; day-to-day work uses `SYSADMIN`.
Use `IDENTIFIER()` with bind variables in admin scripts instead of string concatenation.
Provider versions are pinned with `~>` ranges and updated by a scheduled PR.
Intermediate models are `int_<entity>__<verb>`, e.g. `int_orders__joined_to_customers`.
Action items from postmortems are tracked as tickets with a due date, not prose.
Lock files are regenerated only by the `deps-bump` workflow.
Model artifacts live in the registry; nothing is deployed from a notebook.
Notebooks reading more than 1 GB sample first with `limit` and note the sample in a markdown cell.
Threads: 8 for prod builds, 4 for CI, 2 for local development.
Macros that emit SQL return a string; macros that emit values return via `{{ return() }}`.
Seeds are for small static lookups under 1,000 rows; anything larger lands through the loader, not a CSV in git.
Use `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` for queue-style tables.
Reporting-layer models are prefixed `rpt_` and are one-per-dashboard.
Plan output is attached to the PR; apply happens from CI after approval.
Snowflake load tables use TIMESTAMP_NTZ; do not mix TIMESTAMP_NTZ and TIMESTAMP_TZ in one table.
Do not hardcode dates in marts; use `var('as_of_date')` so backfills are reproducible.
Document the grain and the primary key in every contract.
Use `functools.cache` only on pure functions with hashable arguments.
Rename an Airflow DAG by creating a new `dag_id` and pausing the old one; renaming in place orphans run history.
Import existing resources before managing them; do not recreate in place.
Do not echo secrets even masked; use `::add-mask::` for derived values.
Access to production consoles is via the bastion with session recording.
Check bloat on `sessions` monthly with `pgstattuple` and schedule a repack if over 30%.
Feature stores expose point-in-time-correct joins only; no latest-value shortcuts.
dbt generic tests live in `tests/generic/`; singular tests are for one-off business rules.
Cache pip installs keyed on the hash of the requirements file, not on the branch name.
Grant privileges to roles, never to users; user grants fail the audit.
Docs are generated nightly and published to the internal docs site.
Seed `column_types` for lookup seeds go in `seeds/lookups/_lookups.yml`, one entry per non-text column.
Embeddings are regenerated only when the encoder version changes; store the version.
Set a random seed in the first code cell of any notebook that samples or trains.
Announce schema or contract changes in #data-consumers before merging.
Contract files record an owner, a freshness SLA in hours and an escalation channel for the dataset.
Shares to partners are created from a dedicated `share_*` database with secure views only.
A reviewer re-runs any analysis cited in a decision memo before the memo goes out.
Jobs that touch the warehouse use the `ci_runner` role with a 15-minute query timeout.
Connector secrets are rotated in the secrets manager; connectors read them on start.
`S3KeySensor` waiting on an origin system's file arrival uses `mode='reschedule'` and a 6-hour timeout.
No bare `except:`; catch the narrowest exception and log context.
Include a sample payload in each contract for consumer onboarding.
Row-count drift of more than 5% day over day in a mart raises a `warn` via `dbt_expectations`.
Profile with `py-spy` before optimizing; attach the flame graph to the PR.
Prefer CTEs to subqueries; name them for what they hold, not their position.
Hex or Deepnote notebooks follow the same parameter and secrets rules as local ones.
Long-term storage pricing kicks in at 90 days; do not rewrite old partitions needlessly.
Distribution checks use quantiles rather than means for skewed fields.
Post-incident reviews are written within three business days and name an owner for every corrective action.
Avoid `apply` with row-wise Python functions on frames over 100k rows.
Use `pathlib.Path` for filesystem paths in scripts instead of string concatenation with `os.path`.
Macros must not call `run_query` at parse time; guard anything that touches the warehouse with `{% if execute %}`.
Add a unique test on the first column of each lookup seed.
Macros that query `information_schema` cache results with `{% set cached = ... %}` per run.
Notebooks must not keep timestamp-bearing output cells; clear outputs with `nbstripout` before commit.
Sales region mappings live in `seeds/lookups/lkp_region.csv` and are owned by RevOps.
Terraform resources are named `<env>_<domain>_<kind>`.
Fact models in marts are named `fct_<verb_noun>` and dimensions `dim_<entity>`; a mart table without one of those prefixes does not ship.
Do not use `depends_on_past`; make tasks idempotent instead.
Run `dbt deps` in the image build, not at job start.
Draft PRs are for early feedback; mark ready only when CI is green.
Connections go through PgBouncer in transaction mode; avoid session-level state.
Airflow connections for each origin system are named `src_<system>_<env>`; hosts are never hardcoded in DAG files.
Use parameterized queries; string-built SQL from user input is rejected in review.
Introduce yourself to each consuming team during the first quarter.
Cost anomaly alerts are Snowflake tasks writing to the `ops.alerts` table.
Use threads for follow-ups; one top-level message per topic.
Hide join keys with `hidden: yes`; expose clean dimensions instead.
`TRANSFORM_WH` has a dedicated resource monitor and an owner listed in `snowflake/warehouses.yml`.
Data product pages include a contact, a changelog, and known limitations.
Dataset-triggered DAGs are preferred over cron offsets for downstream dependencies.
BI service accounts have read-only access and a query timeout of five minutes.
LookML views mirror one mart each; derived tables need platform approval.
Pre-commit runs `gitleaks`; a hit blocks the commit.
Prefer `polars` for transforms over 1 GB; `pandas` only for small frames.
Create indexes `CONCURRENTLY` on tables above 1M rows.
Read replicas serve reporting; writes never target a replica endpoint.
Python 3.12 is the floor; do not add `from __future__` imports for older versions.
Duplicate-key checks run on every mart's surrogate key after each build.
Mart SQL is formatted with `sqlfluff` using the repo `.sqlfluff`; CI rejects unformatted files.
Put credentials in Airflow connections, never in DAG files or Variables.
Notebook imports are grouped: stdlib, third party, then `src.` modules.
Use `dbt retry` after transient failures instead of rerunning the whole job.
Macros wrapping warehouse-specific functions live in `macros/adapters/` and define a `default__` implementation as the fallback.
Use `--warn-error-options` in CI so deprecations fail the build.
Notebooks restart-and-run-all cleanly before commit; CI executes them with `papermill`.
Every warehouse is attached to a resource monitor that notifies at 80 percent and suspends at 100 percent of its credit quota.
Table aliases in joins are the initials of the model, e.g. `fo` for `fct_orders`.
Deprecate a mart by setting `deprecation_date` in its yml one release before removing it.
Joins in mart models are written with explicit `inner` or `left` types, with a comment whenever a fan-out is intended.
Every DAG sets `catchup=False`, `max_active_runs=1` and an explicit `owner` in `default_args`.
Kill queries running over two hours unless they are on the allowlist.
Source-system owner contacts are listed in `docs/systems.md`; ask them before changing a connector schedule.
Add a `where` filter inside the snapshot select, not in the downstream view, to cut storage.
Delete unused tables flagged by the 90-day no-access report after owner confirmation.
Hooks that grant privileges run in `on-run-end` and are idempotent.
Use short-lived tokens for CI; no long-lived personal access tokens.
`dim_date` is the only date spine; marts join to it instead of generating their own calendars.
New data vendors need a security review, a DPA, and a cost estimate before a trial.
Use `Decimal` for exact arithmetic in reconciliation scripts; floats are not acceptable there.
Docs pages start with the audience and the outcome, then the steps.
A notebook that backs a decision links its commit hash in the decision doc.
Sensitive-data scans run weekly and open tickets for untagged PII.
Commit messages use backticks around identifiers and tool names.
Dataset `ml_features` has an owner label and a documented retention in `bigquery/datasets.yml`.
Pass data between tasks by path or table name via XCom; never push dataframes.
Evaluate on a time-based split; random splits are not acceptable for forecasting problems.
Runbooks live next to the system in `runbooks/` and are tested during game days.
Transient tables are the default in dev and scratch schemas to save fail-safe storage.
Tables of config values name the default and the unit.
Time travel retention is 7 days for marts schemas and 1 day for scratch.
Loosening a contract constraint needs sign-off from every consuming team listed in the contract.
Every macro has a unit test in `tests/macros/` using `dbt-unit-testing` or an equivalent.
Never edit rows in a snapshot table by hand; open an incident and restore from a clone.
Certified datasets carry a badge and are the default in BI explores.
Stacked PRs name the parent in the title: `[2/3] ...`.
Lookup seeds with more than 20 columns are split by subject area.
Autovacuum settings are tuned per table for any table with over 10M updates a day.
Aim for p95 query cost under 0.1 credits for dashboards.
Date-only columns in marts end with `_date`.
Flaky tests are quarantined with a `@flaky` marker and a ticket; they cannot stay longer than two weeks.
Sensors run in `reschedule` mode so they do not hold worker slots.
Drift in categorical values triggers a review of accepted_values tests.
Profiles for CI and prod are rendered from templates in the deploy job; no profiles in git.
Unit tests run in under 30 seconds in total; slower tests are marked `integration`.
Name resources with the module's `name_prefix` input for consistent naming.
Dashboards read from mart tables or governed explores only, never from raw tables.
Every macro under `macros/` opens with a Jinja comment block stating its purpose, its arguments and one example call.
Scheduled deliveries go to groups, not individuals, and have a named owner.
Prefer boring technology; a new tool needs an ADR and a named owner.
Account usage views lag up to 3 hours; do not alert on them for real-time needs.
Put DAG documentation in `doc_md` with a runbook link.
Use `FUTURE GRANTS` on schemas so new tables are readable by the right roles.
Log prompt, response, and latency for LLM calls with PII redacted.

Analyses start with a comment header naming the requester and the ticket number.
`contract: enforced` is set on mart models only; every mart column declares a `data_type` in the model yml.

Secrets live in the secrets manager; none in git, env files, or chat.
Pin the macro package versions in `packages.yml` and review upgrade diffs in macros/overrides.
Flaky test policy: quarantine, ticket, fix within two weeks, or delete.
Notebook parameters sit in the first cell tagged `parameters`.
SQL keywords are lowercase; one clause per line; trailing commas are not used.
Check bloat on `audit_log` monthly with `pgstattuple` and schedule a repack if over 30%.

Use the `bq` CLI with `--dry_run` to estimate bytes before running a new backfill.

Share notebook results as rendered HTML in the ticket, not as an attached .ipynb.
Version suffixes `_v2` are allowed only during migrations and removed after.
Folders are organized by team; the `Shared` folder is for governed content only.
Check-strategy snapshots list explicit `check_cols`; `all` is rejected in review.

Use `count(*)` for rows and `count(col)` only when you want non-null counts.
Log LLM and API call costs per job and review them monthly.
Onboarding docs are tested by each new hire; they fix what is wrong in their first week.
Cherry-pick hotfixes with `-x` so the origin commit is recorded.
Post the ticket link whenever you ask for review in the channel.
Mart models are `table` or `incremental`; never `view`, because BI tools hit them directly.
Parametrize similar cases instead of copy-pasting tests.
Load jobs from GCS use `WRITE_APPEND` plus a dedupe model, never `WRITE_TRUNCATE` on shared tables.
Docstrings use Google style; examples must be runnable doctests where cheap.

Cache warmed queries for dashboards are defined as exports in the semantic layer.
Consumers register in `contracts/consumers.yml`; producers check it before breaking changes.
Incremental marts set `on_schema_change: append_new_columns` and run a weekly full refresh.
Service accounts authenticate with key-pair auth and a network policy; password logins are reserved for humans.
Alert callbacks post to the owning team's channel with the DAG id, task id and a link to the log, not to a shared catch-all channel.
Do not paste production data into AI assistants or public tools.
Alert fatigue review monthly: any alert that fired more than ten times without action is tuned or removed.
Airflow DAG ids and dbt tags use the same domain names.
Prefer provider-managed `DockerOperator` retries over custom retry loops inside the callable.
Do not expose raw measures that are only building blocks; mark them hidden.
Announce breaking changes in #data-consumers with a date, an impact, and a migration note.
Use `exists` for membership checks on large tables, not `in (select ...)`.
Every `fct_` model has a `Grain:` line in its yml description and a unique test on its surrogate key.
Mart columns that hold PII get `meta: {pii: true}` in the yml so the catalog masks them.
The `Support Load` dashboard is reviewed quarterly by its owner; stale tiles are removed.
Tags use semver with a `v` prefix: `v1.12.0`.
Mart column order: keys first, then attributes, then measures.
Cross-project refs use dbt Mesh with public models only.
Set `invalidate_hard_deletes: true` on snapshots of tables whose source physically deletes rows.
Semantic validation (`dbt sl validate`) runs in CI for every PR touching the semantic layer.
Prefer provider-managed `KubernetesPodOperator` retries over custom retry loops inside the callable.
Status emoji convention: eyes means looking, check means done, warning means blocked.
Property-based tests with `hypothesis` cover parsers and validators.
Use `actions/upload-artifact` retention of 7 days for test logs.
Don't mutate dataframes in place inside helpers; return a new frame.
Run `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` and paste the plan in the PR for any new query on a large table.
`dbt debug` output is attached to environment-related bug reports.
Export limits: 50k rows for CSV; larger asks go through a data request ticket.
File-based loads use checksums and keep the original file for 30 days.
Pin Python dependencies with `==` and let a dedicated bump PR update them, never a feature PR.
Avoid global state in modules imported by Airflow; it leaks between task runs.
Commit messages follow conventional commits: `type: [TICKET] description`.
Egress between regions is billed; keep consumers in the data's region.
Set `temperature=0` for extraction and classification tasks.
Postmortem docs are stored in `docs/postmortems/` with the date in the file name.
Each monitor has an owner and a runbook link in its description.
Reverse ETL syncs read mart tables only; never point a sync at an `int_` model.
Mart models do not select from other marts with `ref()`; share logic through an `int_` model.
Third-party GitHub actions are allowlisted by the security team.
Seeds under `seeds/lookups/` are materialized into the `reference` schema.
Deploy jobs upload `manifest.json` to the artifact store for slim CI and docs.
Cross-project queries reference projects by variable in dbt, not by hardcoded id.
Environment names are `dev`, `ci`, `preprod`, `prod`; no other spellings.
TOAST-heavy tables get their own tablespace monitoring.
Stream large API responses with pagination generators instead of loading them whole.
Alerts channels are muted by default; only @oncall mentions interrupt.
Dataset `marts` has an owner label and a documented retention in `bigquery/datasets.yml`.
Group related tasks with `TaskGroup`; do not add new `SubDagOperator` usage.
Squash fixup commits before merge; `git rebase -i --autosquash`.
Promote a build from the staging environment to prod only after approval in #data-release.
Lookup seeds hold at most 5,000 rows; larger reference data loads through the ingestion pipeline.
Right-size Airflow workers quarterly using utilization graphs.
BI column labels for mart fields are Title Case and omit warehouse jargon.
Variables in `dbt_project.yml` are lowercase with underscores and documented.
Dev schemas are `dbt_<username>`; they are not shared between people.
Store admin DDL in `snowflake/ddl/` and apply it through Terraform or schemachange only.
Marts materialized as `table` use `+on_configuration_change: apply` to avoid full rebuilds.
Table `accounts` has a documented retention and an index review date in `postgres/tables.md`.
A TODO in code must reference a ticket.
Snapshot targets use `target_schema: snapshots` with `+persist_docs` enabled.
Spark jobs set `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions` explicitly for large joins.
Prefer provider-managed `SqlSensor` retries over custom retry loops inside the callable.
Warehouse size changes go through Terraform, with the reason in the commit message.
Use `actions/cache` for `~/.cache/pre-commit` to keep lint under a minute.
`BigQueryInsertJobOperator` tasks set an explicit `execution_timeout`; the default of none hangs the scheduler queue.
The `region-eu` and `region-us` metadata views are queried separately; there is no global view.
Join paths between semantic models are one-hop; deeper paths need an intermediate model.
Airflow 2.9 upgrades are rehearsed in the `airflow-sandbox` namespace before touching prod.
`Marketing Funnel` tiles cite the mart they read from in the tile description.
Run `airflow dags test` locally for any DAG change that touches a schedule.
Mart column names use business terms; internal system names stay out of marts.
Environments are separate workspaces or directories, never conditionals in one file.
Experiments log parameters, data version, and git SHA in the tracking server.
Rotate key pairs every 90 days using the `rotate-sf-keys` workflow.
Access requests for dashboards go through the #data-access form, not DMs.
Review slot usage for `analytics` jobs monthly and tag outliers in #data-cost.
A snapshot needs a trustworthy `updated_at` timestamp column in its origin table; otherwise use the `check` strategy.
Review `LOAD_WH` utilization monthly and downsize if average queueing is zero.
Pin the kernel to the repo's `uv` environment, not the base conda environment.
Zero-copy clone prod into `clone_<ticket>` for testing; drop it after seven days.
Join conditions use explicit `on` clauses; implicit comma joins are rejected.
Stop the bleeding first: pause the DAG or revert the deploy before diagnosing.
Use `for_each` over `count` when resources have identities.
Mart models use `{{ config(tags=['nightly']) }}` or `['hourly']`; untagged marts never run in prod.
Each dataset in the catalog has an owner, description, and update cadence.
Small PRs, frequent merges; long-lived branches are a smell.
Review `ADHOC_WH` utilization monthly and downsize if average queueing is zero.
Version docs per release for tools that have versioned behavior.
Major version upgrades are rehearsed on a restored clone with production-like load.
Use `--target ci` locally to reproduce CI failures exactly.
Snowflake stages for COPY INTO use a storage integration; never embed cloud keys in a stage definition.
Clear a failed task rather than triggering a fresh DAG run, so lineage stays intact.
Columns tagged `pii` get a masking policy applied in Terraform, never by hand in the console.
Never put customer data in a seed; seeds are public in the repo.
Scripting blocks in scheduled queries declare variables at the top and avoid dynamic SQL.
Use advisory locks for singleton jobs, with a documented lock id range.
Time-box spikes to two days and report findings even if inconclusive.
Referential checks run between facts and dimensions nightly with sampled failure rows saved.
Store snapshot configs in the snapshot file, not in `dbt_project.yml`.
Reusable workflows live in `.github/workflows/reusable-*.yml` and are versioned by tag.
Custom generic tests live in `tests/generic/`, are named `test_<assertion>`, and ship with a passing and a failing fixture.
Pytest fixtures that open a warehouse connection are session-scoped and use a read-only role.
Column descriptions are inherited from upstream docs where possible, not retyped.
Lookup seeds must not be referenced by snapshots.
Dataset `finance_ro` has an owner label and a documented retention in `bigquery/datasets.yml`.
PII columns are tagged and masked by default; unmask requires approval and is logged.
Cost per query goes in the PR description for any new scheduled workload.
A tile that takes over 20 seconds gets a ticket for model or aggregate work.
Do not use `select distinct` to fix duplicates in a mart; fix the join grain upstream.
Model refresh frequency follows consumer need; hourly refresh needs a named consumer.
Partition large tables by ingestion date and require a partition filter.
Use `pg_dump --schema-only` diffs in review for hand-written DDL.
Snapshots select from a stable model via `ref()`, never from a view whose row set changes between runs.
A singular test returns failing rows and carries a comment explaining the rule.
Analyses that become recurring are promoted to a mart through a normal PR.
YAML for mart models declares `meta.owner` with a team name, and mart column descriptions state business meaning rather than the SQL.
Prefer provider-managed `HttpOperator` retries over custom retry loops inside the callable.
Use the `logging` module with a module-level logger in scripts; bare `print` is reserved for CLI output.
Don't use `SERIAL` for new tables; use identity columns.

Quarterly governance review checks the top 50 datasets by query volume.
Use `git mv` for file moves so history follows the file.
`fct_` and `dim_` prefixes are lowercase; the entity part is singular for dims and plural for facts.
Golden-file tests update only via an explicit `--update-golden` flag and a reviewed diff.
Ad-hoc warehouses set `auto_suspend` to 60 seconds and `auto_resume` to true.
Division uses `nullif(denominator, 0)` to avoid divide-by-zero errors.
Changes under `models/marts/finance/` need a review from the finance analytics engineer listed in CODEOWNERS.
Document each module with an example in its README.
File names in `analyses/` are free-form but lowercase with underscores.
Keep `CODEOWNERS` current; a PR changing an unowned path fails the check.
Build docs in CI and fail on broken links with `lychee`.
Python scripts parse timestamp strings with `datetime.fromisoformat`, not `strptime` with ad hoc formats.
Python models end with `_py` so engineers know they run on a different compute path.
A mart that joins more than five models needs a lineage diagram in its yml `description`.
Documentation owners are listed in `CODEOWNERS` for each docs folder.
Connectors run with least-privilege read-only credentials on the origin system.
Version numbers appear in the contract file name suffix: `orders_v2.yaml`.
The security team owns the allowlist for outbound network destinations.
Materialized views are not used; dynamic tables or dbt incrementals replace them.
Test migrations on a copy of prod data volume before the release window.
Analysis authors list the warehouse role they ran it with in the header comment.
Record questions you had in week one in the FAQ page for the next hire.
`Revenue Overview` tiles cite the mart they read from in the tile description.
Changelogs follow Keep a Changelog and are updated in release PRs.
Table `audit_log` has a documented retention and an index review date in `postgres/tables.md`.
Dashboards unused for 90 days are archived automatically; owners are notified first.
Announce a backfill in the data-incidents channel with the date range and models before running it.
Macro names are verbs: `get_`, `generate_`, `build_`; helpers never start with an underscore.
Dashboard performance is checked with the Looker `i__looker` usage explore monthly.
Check bloat on `accounts` monthly with `pgstattuple` and schedule a repack if over 30%.
Batch scoring jobs write predictions with the model version in a column.
`ADHOC_WH` has a dedicated resource monitor and an owner listed in `snowflake/warehouses.yml`.
Cluster by up to four columns, ordered by filter frequency.

CI model selection uses `state:modified+` against the prod manifest; `--select *` is rejected for PR builds.
Embed dashboards use signed URLs with a one-hour expiry.
Net revenue is defined once under `models/marts/finance/` and reused; do not recompute it inside a downstream mart or BI model.
Tag every warehouse and project with `cost_center`; untagged spend is billed to platform.
Plots in notebooks set axis labels and units; unlabeled charts are rejected in review.
BigQuery fact tables are partitioned by the DATE of the event timestamp and require a partition filter.
Use sparklines sparingly; every chart must answer a stated question.
Pin one canonical dashboard per department on the homepage.
Add columns as nullable first, backfill in batches, then add `NOT NULL` in a later migration.
Hyperparameter sweeps are capped at 50 trials without approval.
Schedule heavy jobs off-peak; the BI-hours window is 08:00 to 18:00 local.
A new connector needs a design review, a cost estimate, and a runbook.
`Support Load` tiles cite the mart they read from in the tile description.
Multi-cluster warehouses cap `MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT` at 3 unless approved in #data-cost.
Deprecate a dashboard by adding a banner for two weeks before archiving.
Avoid `select *` from wide joins; list the columns you need.
Run `dbt snapshot` before `dbt run` in the nightly job, and never run snapshots in PR CI builds.
Budget alerts at 50%, 80% and 100% go to #data-cost.
Public buckets are banned; the nightly scanner opens an incident on any exposure.
Table `sessions` has a documented retention and an index review date in `postgres/tables.md`.
Check bloat on `events` monthly with `pgstattuple` and schedule a repack if over 30%.
Run a game day per quarter that simulates a warehouse outage.
Never schedule notebooks directly; wrap them in a DAG task using papermill.
Table `users` has a documented retention and an index review date in `postgres/tables.md`.
Column-level security uses policy tags from the `pii` taxonomy.
Do not DM for support questions; ask in #data-help so answers are searchable.
Share analysis queries through the repo, not screenshots, so others can rerun them.
Set `STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS` to 1800 on transform warehouses and 300 on BI.
Snapshots are the only place we keep history; never rebuild one with `--full-refresh`.
Service accounts are named `svc-<system>-<purpose>` and owned by a team alias.
Backfill runs suppress anomaly alerts for the backfilled range only.
Use `qualify` instead of nested subqueries for row-number filters where the warehouse supports it.
Each metric has a description, a type, and an owner in the yml.
Workflows declare `permissions: contents: read` at the top and widen it per job only when needed.
Ownership changes are updated in the catalog the same day a team reorganizes.
Reserved capacity commitments are reviewed by finance and platform twice a year.

Run `sqlfluff lint` only on changed `.sql` files in PRs, all files on main.

Generated client code from contracts is never edited by hand.

Review snapshot diffs with a sample of 20 changed keys pasted in the PR description.

Schema changes go through Alembic migrations with both upgrade and downgrade.
Cap CI warehouse spend at 5% of the monthly total; alert beyond that.

Drift reports run weekly on the top 20 features and post to #ml-ops.

Communicate in plain language: what is wrong, who is affected, what we are doing.

Squash-merge feature PRs; keep merge commits only for release branches.
A mart change that drops a column needs a deprecation notice in #data-consumers a week ahead.
Roll back a bad deploy by reverting the PR, not by hot-patching production.
Notebooks never hold production logic: scheduled work moves to a DAG or a dbt model before it ships.
Semantic model yml lives next to the mart it describes.
Vendor API clients live in `src/clients/` with one module per vendor.
Name CTEs in analyses after the business concept (`active_accounts`), not `a`, `b` or `tmp`.
Webhook receivers verify signatures before enqueuing payloads.
Contract YAML is linted in CI before merge.
Rotate service credentials every 90 days; automation owns rotation.
Vendor tools are reviewed annually; unused seats are cancelled.
Scheduled workflows post failures to the data-alerts channel instead of relying on email notifications.
Foreign keys are indexed on the referencing column.
Seed lookups are prefixed `lkp_`; do not reuse the prefix elsewhere.
Temporary models for backfills are prefixed `tmp_` and removed after the backfill.
Estimate with ranges and update them when you learn something.
Task ids use snake_case verbs: `load_orders`, `run_dbt_build`.
Monitor lag per topic and partition; alert at 10 minutes for tier-1 streams.
Review the 20 most expensive queries each month and file a ticket for any that grew more than 30 percent.
Prefer `dataclasses` or `pydantic` over positional tuples for returning multiple values.
Self-hosted runners are used for warehouse-connected jobs; hosted runners for lint.
Seat counts for tools are reviewed quarterly and trimmed.
`--full-refresh` in prod needs a ticket and a second approver.
The `Ops Daily` dashboard is reviewed quarterly by its owner; stale tiles are removed.
Keep notebook data files out of git; reference warehouse tables or object-store paths.
Parquet exports to the data lake write timestamp columns as int64 microseconds; isoformat strings are CSV-only.
Measures declare a `value_format_name` and a one-line description.
Postgres: rename a column behind a view shim for one release; never `ALTER ... RENAME` on a table readers use.
Integration tests use the `ci` schema and clean up what they create.
Tests that need network access are marked and skipped by default locally.
PRs stay under 400 changed lines; larger changes are split into stacked PRs.
Shadow-deploy a new model for a week before switching traffic.
Use `freezegun` or an injected clock; tests never depend on the current time.
Test DAG integrity with `pytest tests/dags/test_dag_integrity.py` before deploying.
Test data never contains real customer records.
Don't change unrelated things during an incident; one change at a time with a note.
Grant `MONITOR` on warehouses to analysts so they can self-diagnose slow queries.
Shadow an on-call shift before joining the rotation.
Encoding is UTF-8 end to end; reject files that fail decoding instead of replacing characters.
Keep PRs under about 400 changed lines; larger changes are split into a refactor PR and a behavior PR.
Prefer provider-managed `EmailOperator` retries over custom retry loops inside the callable.
Dashboard exposures live in `models/marts/_exposures.yml`, each with an owner email and a maturity of high, medium or low.
Rebase onto main before requesting review; resolve conflicts locally.
Intermediate models are prefixed `int_`, live in `models/intermediate/`, and are never granted to BI roles.
Log manual production fixes in `ops/manual-changes.md` with the SQL used.
CLI tools use `typer`; arguments have help text and a documented default.
Set `statement_timeout` to 30s for app roles and 15min for reporting roles.
Slot reservations are assigned per project; the `etl` project gets baseline 500 slots.
Use `is_` or `has_` prefixes for boolean flags in marts.
Delete merged branches; the `branch-cleanup` workflow runs weekly.
Modules are versioned and pinned by tag; no `ref=main`.
Snapshot (approval) tests store expected output next to the test.
Name notebooks `YYYY-MM-DD_<author>_<topic>.ipynb`; a notebook reused twice is promoted to a script or model.
Required checks: lint, unit tests, `dbt parse`, and `dbt build` in the ci schema.
Branch names are `<type>/<ticket>-<slug>`, e.g. `feat/PROJ-123-add-retry`.
Use fixtures with small deterministic data; no live warehouse in unit tests.
Boolean columns in lookup seeds use `true`/`false`, never `Y`/`N`.
Protect `main` with required reviews and linear history.
Workflow files have a header comment explaining when they run and who owns them.
Cumulative metrics state their window in the metric name.
Notebook code that is reused moves into `src/<package>/` with tests.
Each snapshot has a `unique_key` that is a single column; build it in the upstream model if needed.
Mart documentation blocks live in `models/marts/docs.md` and are referenced with `{{ doc() }}`.
Scripts run under `python -m` from the repo root; no `sys.path` edits.
One incident commander at a time; hand off explicitly in the channel.
Dimension models expose exactly one current row per natural key; history lives in `snapshots/`.
Contract-enforced mart models list every column with a `data_type`, and the build fails if the query returns an extra column.
Table `invoices_app` has a documented retention and an index review date in `postgres/tables.md`.
Read the three most recent postmortems in the first month.
Warehouse roles are `<domain>_ro` and `<domain>_rw`.
Data warehouse grants managed in Terraform are not edited in the console.
Dependabot PRs are grouped weekly and merged by the platform team only.
Sunset notices for a contract go to every registered consumer and the data-consumers channel.
Snapshots write to the `snapshots` schema and the file name equals the snapshot name, one snapshot per file.
Permissions are group-based and mirrored from the IdP groups nightly.
Use `%sql` magics only against the read-only `analytics_ro` role.
Use `pydantic` models for config files, not raw dicts.
Explores join mart models only; a LookML view pointing at an intermediate model fails review.
Batch updates in chunks of 10k rows with a sleep between chunks.
Terraform plans run in CI on every PR touching `terraform/`; apply only from main.
Scripts read warehouse credentials with `os.environ["NAME"]` and no default.
Airflow 2.10 upgrades are rehearsed in the `airflow-sandbox` namespace before touching prod.
Tableau extracts refresh after the dbt job via the webhook, not on a fixed clock.
Use `jsonb`, not `json`, and index only the paths you query.
Heavy analyses run on the `analytics_xl` warehouse only after a #data-cost heads up.
Table `events` has a documented retention and an index review date in `postgres/tables.md`.
Contract freshness SLAs are monitored and breaches post to #data-contracts.
Late-arriving changes are handled by re-running the snapshot, not by editing the history table.
Variables have descriptions and types; unused variables are removed.
Retrospective actions older than 60 days without progress are escalated.
A dashboard that executives open at 8am being stale or wrong is a Sev1 and pages the on-call engineer.
Raw landing tables are append-only; loaders never update them in place.
`SnowflakeOperator` tasks set an explicit `execution_timeout`; the default of none hangs the scheduler queue.
Review slot usage for `ml_features` jobs monthly and tag outliers in #data-cost.
Logical decoding consumers use `pgoutput` and a dedicated replication role.
Add an optional field in a minor version; removing or retyping a field is major.
Commit `requirements.lock` updates in a separate PR from feature code.
Contracts are YAML files in `contracts/`, one per published dataset, owned by the producing team.
Search the catalog before creating a new dataset; duplicates are merged or justified.
A DAG owner must be a team alias, never an individual email.
Event schemas are validated at the edge; invalid events go to a quarantine topic.
Use `pytest.mark.parametrize` ids that read well in failures.
Demo features to consumers before declaring them done.
Backfills after an incident are announced in #data-consumers with the affected date range.
Analyses that ran longer than ten minutes get a comment with the warehouse size used.
Write in present tense and active voice; avoid 'simply' and 'just'.
Snapshots get a not_null test on `dbt_valid_from` and a unique test on `dbt_scd_id`.
Type-annotate public functions; `mypy --strict` runs on `src/` in CI.
Dead-letter queues are monitored; an item older than 24 hours pages the owner.
Index, constraint and table names stay under 63 characters.
IAM policies are least-privilege, written in HCL, not pasted JSON.
Every PR description lists what changed, why, and how it was tested.
New warehouses default to X-Small; sizing up needs a ticket that cites the query it speeds up.
Test a snapshot change in a clone of prod, never in the shared dev schema.
Draft contracts are merged with `status: draft` and cannot be consumed by production jobs.
Do not assert on log text; assert on structured fields.
A contract owner is a team, not an individual; the team alias must exist in the directory.
Dev databases are named `DEV_<USER>`; they are cleaned up when the user leaves.
Test restores of encrypted backups quarterly with the key custodian present.
Production runs use `dbt build` with selectors from `selectors.yml`, not ad hoc flags.
Use `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS` to find the top 20 queries by bytes billed each week.
Landing buckets have lifecycle rules: 30 days hot, 1 year cold.
LookML refinements are used for per-team tweaks; do not fork views.
Use the `timestamp` snapshot strategy when the source has a trustworthy `updated_at`; fall back to `check` only when it does not.
Each dataset in the catalog has a steward, a description, and a freshness expectation.
Never use a macro to hide a join; joins stay visible in model SQL.
BI Engine reservations are sized by the BI team and reviewed quarterly.
Dry-run destructive commands and paste the output in the ticket.
Buddy assignments last 30 days; buddies review the first three PRs.
Dynamic task mapping is capped at 256 mapped tasks per run.
File drops include a manifest with row counts; loaders reject mismatches.
Every contract lists an on-call contact and escalation channel.
Sensors run in `mode="reschedule"` with an explicit `timeout`.
Use `APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT` for dashboards; exact counts only for reconciliations.
Filters on metrics use dimension names, not column names.
Put ticket-specific date ranges in one `{% set %}` block at the top of an analysis instead of scattering literals through the query.
A new engineer's first production change is paired and low risk.
Notebooks over 20 cells are split or promoted into a script.
Use `git bisect` with a failing test before opening a regression ticket.
Do not use seeds for secrets, API keys, or hostnames.
Labels `team`, `env` and `pipeline` are required on datasets and scheduled queries.
Dev credentials expire after 90 days; the onboarding doc explains renewal.
Dataset `raw_events` has an owner label and a documented retention in `bigquery/datasets.yml`.
Declare an incident in #data-incidents with severity, impact, and an owner within 15 minutes.
Hooks (`on-run-start`, `on-run-end`) call macros; never inline SQL in `dbt_project.yml`.
Data transfer jobs use service account impersonation, not keys.
Artifacts older than 30 days are expired by the storage lifecycle rule.
Submodules are not allowed; vendor or package dependencies instead.
Weekly office hours with the platform team are the place for design questions.
Contract-specific quality rules live next to the contract, not in the pipeline code.
Volume monitors alert when daily row counts deviate by more than three standard deviations.
Use `SAFE_CAST` in ad hoc exploration but plain `CAST` in pipelines so bad data fails loudly.
LLM prompts are stored in the repo with a version and an evaluation set.
Lookup seeds are changed in their own PR so reviewers can diff the data.
Access requests link the catalog entry and the business justification.
Snapshot yml renames `dbt_valid_to` to `valid_to` via `snapshot_meta_column_names`, never in downstream models.
Snapshot tables keep 400 days of closed rows; a monthly job archives the rest to cold storage.
Saved queries cover the top 10 dashboard asks and are tested in CI.
Glossary terms are defined once in `docs/glossary.md` and linked elsewhere.
Overrides of dbt-core macros live in `macros/overrides/` with a link to the upstream macro.
`BashOperator` tasks set an explicit `execution_timeout`; the default of none hangs the scheduler queue.
Screenshots are avoided in favor of text; if used, they need alt text.
Never delete evidence: snapshot logs and query history before cleaning up.
Mart folders set `+materialized: table` once in `dbt_project.yml`, and mart models do not repeat it in their own config blocks.
Non-additive measures declare how they aggregate across time.
Retention policy is recorded per dataset and enforced by scheduled jobs.
A new macro is merged only together with a unit test under `tests/generic/` or `unit_tests/` that exercises it.
Use on-demand pricing in dev and editions reservations in prod.
Decision logs are append-only; supersede instead of editing.
Do not train on data younger than the label delay window.
Diagrams are text-based (Mermaid) so they can be reviewed in diffs.
Never force-push a branch that has an open review; add fixup commits and let the squash-merge tidy history.
Compute for notebooks auto-stops after 30 minutes idle.
Data classification labels are mandatory on new datasets: public, internal, restricted.
Local `dev` target builds into the personal schema with `--defer --favor-state`.
Lookup seed files use the `lkp_` prefix and a singular noun: `lkp_country`, `lkp_plan_tier`.
PII fields are flagged in the contract and mapped to the retention policy.
Document each snapshot's owner and retention in `snapshots/_snapshots.yml`.
Hide surrogate keys from the field picker with `hidden: yes` and set `primary_key: yes` on the view's key.
CI posts the dbt run summary as a PR comment, updating it rather than adding a new one.
Every lookup seed has a README row in `seeds/lookups/_lookups.yml` naming the business owner.
Snapshot yml declares `dbt_valid_to_current` as `9999-12-31` so range joins stay index friendly.
Release notes go out every Friday with links to merged PRs.
Mart columns exposed to finance carry `meta.certified: true` only after the owning team signs off in the PR.
Backups use point-in-time recovery with a 14-day window; restore drills run quarterly.
Prefer one right-sized warehouse over many idle ones.
Never call `datetime.now()` in a DAG file; use the `data_interval_start` template variable.
Macros that loop over columns use `adapter.get_columns_in_relation` and skip when `execute` is false.
Macros take named arguments with defaults once they have more than three parameters, instead of a long positional list.
Packages are upgraded monthly in a dedicated PR with the changelog linked.
Dashboards show a 'data as of' footer sourced from the mart load log.
Connection limits per role are set explicitly; the default is unlimited.
Use `pg_repack` rather than `VACUUM FULL` on live tables.
Temporary access grants expire automatically; extension needs a new request.
Partition tables by range once they pass 100M rows; keep 13 months online.
Suppressions of alerts expire in 14 days and need a reason.
Lock timeouts of 5s apply to migrations so they fail fast instead of blocking traffic.
The catalog is the only place we publish SLAs; wiki copies are removed.
Test contract changes against a consumer sample before merging.
Clear all cell outputs before committing a notebook.
Lookup seeds are named `ref_<topic>` and keep one code per row with its human label alongside.
Do not disable TLS verification, even for internal test endpoints.
Secrets are passed as environment variables to the step that needs them, not the whole job.
Throttle backfills so they never exceed 30% of the origin database's capacity.
Join #data-help, #data-incidents and #data-release in the first week.
Link tickets from design docs, not the other way around.
Large training jobs checkpoint every 15 minutes so spot interruptions are cheap.
Security reviews are required for new vendors that touch customer data.
Keep test helpers in `tests/helpers/`; do not import them from `src/`.
Use relative links between docs so they survive repo moves.
Capture assumptions in the ticket when requirements are vague.
Export to GCS uses compressed Avro for tables that will be reloaded, CSV only for hand-offs.
A failed backfill is its own incident with its own commander.
A vendor outage triggers the vendor-incident checklist, including consumer notice.
Each vendor integration has an exit plan documenting how to export our data.
Post the result summary of an analysis in the ticket, not in Slack DMs.
